Team —

Thanks again for joining the interview loop for Ethan yesterday. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can make a call on next steps before Monday: 

1) Please upload a filled scorecard (use the attached template) to the candidate folder in Drive and add any short notes inline. If you prefer, attach your completed PDF reply.
2) Call out any clear disqualifying concerns (security, infra fundamentals, or culture fit) explicitly in the first line of your notes.
3) If you recommend an onsite or follow-up system design, say so and list the top 2 areas to probe.

I've attached the raw interview notes I took and the template for scorecards. I'm proposing a short 20-min calibration call today at 4pm PT to align recommendations — if we can't agree we'll default to a 2nd-round take-home + pairing session.

Action items: marissa — your backend deep-dive score; ava — system design call recommendation; karthik — overall hire/no-hire inclination.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-ethan-brooks-notes

Jonas

Jonas —

Attached my completed scorecard (marissa_scorecard_ethan.pdf). TL;DR: strong backend fundamentals, very comfortable with KV stores and caching strategies, but a little light on long-running job orchestration (we had a small mismatch on cron-based workflows).

Disqualifying concerns: none.
Recommend: follow-up 1-hour system design focused on long-running job reliability + scaling KV cache invalidation. If that interview goes well, I lean towards moving to onsite.

Notes: see page 2 for verbatim examples he gave on eventual consistency trade-offs — helpful but shallow in follow-up probing.

—Marissa

Attachment: marissa_scorecard_ethan.pdf

Subject: Re: Ethan Brooks: hire-readiness checklist and interview wrap

Adding my quick scores inline below (full notes in Drive):

- System design (scale & observable retries): 3.5/5 — good high-level choices but missed a couple edge cases around fan-out backpressure.
- Debugging & tooling: 4/5 — solid with traces and sampling strategies.
- Collaboration & communication: 4/5.

Concern: he struggled to justify a rollout strategy for a stateful migration scenario — that would be risky on infra teams that run migrations frequently.

Recommendation: do a targeted 60-min follow-up (onsite-lite) on stateful migration + migration rollbacks. I think a focused follow-up will resolve the unknowns rather than rejecting now.

Thanks,
Ava

Thanks all — consolidated view and proposed next steps: 

Summary: 
- Strengths: dependable backend knowledge, good debugging/tooling instincts, communicates clearly.
- Unknowns: stateful migration strategy + long-running job orchestration.
- Immediate concerns: none are disqualifying.

Proposal: schedule a 60-minute focused follow-up with Jonas + Ava next Wednesday (onsite-lite, remote) to drill migration rollback plan and backpressure handling. If he demonstrates pragmatic strategies, we move to onsite. If gaps remain, we pause and ask the recruiter to source senior candidates with migration experience.

I set a poll for the calibration call and the follow-up slot: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=panel-cal-20270530

- Marissa: paste a 1-line hire/no-hire inclination in GH (REDW-3982) so recruiting can proceed with scheduling.
- Ava/Jonas: confirm availability for the follow-up Wednesday 10am PT or 2pm PT.
- Alisha (cc'd in BCC): hold tentative time until we confirm.

I'll capture final recommendation after the 20-min calibration call; if we can't meet today, we'll go ahead and schedule the follow-up based on the poll.
